assertions.title: Circle rearrangement
assertions.statement_tex:
\label{lem:circle-rearrangement}
Let $q$ be a bounded, nonnegative circle kernel that is even and
nonincreasing as a function of geodesic distance from the origin.
For nonnegative $f,g\in L^1$, let $f^*,g^*$ be their symmetric
decreasing rearrangements. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:circle-rearrangement}
 \iint f(\theta)q(\theta-\phi)g(\phi)
                  \,\dd\mu_1(\theta)\,\dd\mu_1(\phi)
 \le
 \iint f^*(\theta)q(\theta-\phi)g^*(\phi)
                  \,\dd\mu_1(\theta)\,\dd\mu_1(\phi),
\end{equation}
where $\dd\mu_1=\dd\theta/(2\pi)$. Rearrangement preserves
pointwise order and is nonexpansive in $L^1$.
assertions.statement_audit: Complete canonical layer-cake circle rearrangement for arbitrary nonnegative L1 input, with equidistribution, finiteness ae, pointwise radial monotonicity/order, actual double integral inequality and L1 contraction. No smoothness, optimizer, Euler or certificate premise. Registered as target219; main219 build and exact axiom audit passed.
assertions.proof_correspondence_audit: Follows four-point sorting, preservation of Lipschitz bounds, Arzela-Ascoli compactness, common cosine-moment maximization, canonical identification and L1 approximation. L1 contraction is first passed from simultaneous finite polarizations to Lipschitz orbit limits and then to arbitrary L1 limits; the manuscript derives contraction directly from the layer-cake distance identity. Layer-cake representatives are independently identified via exact centered-arc measures and superlevel sets; pointwise order is proved directly for these representatives, including possible infinite values at null radii.

assertions.title: Positive Taylor expansion
assertions.statement_tex:
\label{lem:positive-bernstein}

Suppose $f\in C^\infty([0,1]^{\d})$ and

$\partial^\alpha f\ge0$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, including

$\alpha=0$. Then

\begin{equation}\label{eq:positive-taylor-series}
 f(y)=\sum_{\alpha\in\N_0^{\d}}c_\alpha y^\alpha,
 \qquad
 c_\alpha=\frac{\partial^\alpha f(0)}{\alpha!}\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_\alpha c_\alpha=f(1,\ldots,1),
\end{equation}

where the series converges uniformly on $[0,1]^\d$.
